notes: Needs Docker, a teranode:latest image and a chaos-test checkout at ../chaos-test. Baseline = no skill. Assertions check that the agent uses chaosctl.sh, respects the one-stack rule and asks before destroying state.

evals.name: bring-up-galts-fleet
evals.prompt: Bring up galt's chaos-test fleet so I can run his scenarios.
evals.expected_output: Checks status, brings up Stack B with chaosctl.sh stack up b (asking before --switch if Stack A is running), waits for convergence and reports the fleet, image and orchestrator URL.
assertions: Runs chaosctl.sh stack status before acting
Uses chaosctl.sh stack up b rather than hand-written make/docker commands
If Stack A is running, asks before bringing it down (or the user already said to switch)
Reports whether the fleet converged and the orchestrator URL

evals.name: split-after-freeze
evals.prompt: stack status says SPLIT and teranode1 is one block behind on a different tip after the freeze scenario. What do I do?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the freeze holder refuses the other chain and mining cannot heal it; recommends stack reset and asks before wiping the chain.
assertions: Identifies the split as the expected result of a freeze scenario, not a sync lag
Asks for confirmation before resetting (it deletes the chain)

evals.name: which-stack
evals.prompt: I want to see how the pruner behaves under split-mode service kills while running a scenario. Which stack?
evals.expected_output: Stack A (split mode, pruner rigs, multinode.sh chaos); explains Stack B lacks split mode and Aerospike.
assertions: Does not start or stop anything without being asked
